msg: D-10: motive compile slice-state divergence traced to single-ledger ground truth

data.title: Compile slice-state divergence is a ground-truth scoping defect, not stale ledgers
data.decision: Treat the slice_state_mismatch finding as a defect in motive-ground-truth.mjs readLedger (hooks/lib/motive-ground-truth.mjs:130-175), which selects only the single most-recently-modified file in .groundwork/runs/ and discards the other six ledgers. Slices completed in earlier sessions therefore have no ledger witness, and Progress reconstructs as 0/N complete regardless of recorded completion. Fix direction: union slice state across all ledgers for the motive, keyed by slice id, with later completion winning.
data.rationale: P-B and P-A: the motive spine must reconstruct what actually happened across sessions. A per-session ledger view makes any multi-session motive permanently look unstarted, and emits a high-severity false finding that trains readers to ignore divergence output.

msg: D-12: supersedes D-10 — divergence has two distinct causes; slice ids are session-scoped, so cross-ledger union is unsafe

data.title: Compile slice-state divergence: two causes, and slice ids are not globally unique
data.decision: Supersede D-10. Evidence: readLedger (motive-ground-truth.mjs:130-175) selected .groundwork/runs/63c4ddbe….json (motive undefined, S1/S2/S3 all complete). Its journal shard carries TASK_COMPLETE only for S2 and S3, each with the synthetic motive session:63c4ddbe…. So (a) the high finding is the ledger-complete-without-witness branch (motive-compile.mjs:451-455) firing on S1, which genuinely has no TASK_COMPLETE — the session_completed_ids rescue path works but cannot invent a missing witness; and (b) Progress renders 0/3 because the reconstructed:all_slices path ignores ledger status entirely. These are separate defects and must be diagnosed before either is fixed. Critically, slice ids are reused across sessions (S1..S8 appear in three different ledgers, and plugin-cleanup owns its own S1..S19), so D-10s prescription to union slice state across all ledgers by bare id would silently cross-attribute completions between motives. Any cross-ledger view must key on (session_id, slice_id) and filter by the ledger motive field.
data.rationale: P-B: acting on D-10s mechanism would have produced more false findings and cross-motive contamination. The ledgers motive field being unset is the upstream cause of the synthetic session: motive on TASK_COMPLETE, and is the more likely real fix point.

data.title: Who writes ticket bodies
data.decision: Split authorship along the lifecycle points that already exist, so no new ceremony is introduced (P-D). ORCHESTRATOR/PLANNER at ticket open: Question, Context, Options under consideration, Blocked-by, cross-links — the planner already holds this in-window, so capture is free. IMPLEMENTER (general-purpose) at slice completion: Evidence gathered (with file:line citations), the bold one-sentence Decision, Ruled out and why. ENFORCEMENT rides on an existing call: ledger complete warns (does not block) when the referenced ticket has an empty Question or Decision section. No new pre-work gate.
data.rationale: P-D is decisive precedent: spec-guard.mjs was disabled by its own author because it imposed continuous authoring cost. A design that demands a rich ticket before work may start gets disabled the same way. Warn-on-an-existing-call is one-time capture, not continuous ceremony.

msg: D-28: session pacing is a per-run PACE POLICY in the run ledger, enforced at claim/start time, counted in waves, kind-exempt for non-impl work

data.decision: Session pacing is configured by an additive, optional run-ledger object `pacing` = {policy:"wave"|"slice", budget:N, exempt_kinds:[…], grant:{range,granted_at,granted_by,reason}, resolved:[…]}. Default policy for NEW runs (stamped by `ledger init`): policy=wave, budget=1, exempt_kinds=[plan,diagnose,design,fog]. A UNIT is a wave (policy=wave) or a single non-exempt slice (policy=slice). A unit is RESOLVED when every non-exempt slice in it reaches status=complete. Enforcement is at START time, not completion time: `ledger claim` and `ledger set --status in_progress` exit 1 when the target slice belongs to a NEW unit and resolved_units >= budget + grant.range. Claims into the IN-FLIGHT unit (lowest-numbered unit holding any non-exempt incomplete slice) are always free, which preserves unlimited intra-wave subagent fan-out. Exempt-kind slices are always claimable and never counted. `ledger complete` is NEVER blocked — refusing to record finished work would be a lie in the ledger (P-B). `ledger autopilot --range N [--reason …]` writes pacing.grant, emits a MILESTONE journal event, and expires with the run because it lives in the session-scoped ledger. Policy logic lives in a new pure module hooks/lib/pacing.mjs (resolveUnit/resolvedUnits/inFlightUnit/checkPace -> {allowed,reason,remedy}) so hooks/ledger.mjs, hooks/stop-gate.mjs and hooks/lib/motive-map.mjs are thin disjoint consumers.
data.rationale: Wayfinder-style one-ticket-per-session discipline is the goal, but groundwork fans out many subagents inside one wave; counting slices would forbid the fan-out that makes groundwork fast. Counting WAVES gives the same pacing pressure while leaving intra-wave parallelism untouched. Enforcing at claim time (rather than at complete time) stops wasted work before it happens; the in-flight-unit rule closes the bypass where a session claims everything and completes nothing, without needing a second counter. Kind exemptions mirror wayfinder exempting research tickets: plan/diagnose/design/fog are orientation, not delivery. Absent `pacing` means pacing disabled, so every pre-existing ledger keeps working unchanged (additive-with-sane-default, no shim).
alternatives: Count individual slices with budget=1 — rejected: breaks intra-wave fan-out, the core of the ultrawork model.
Count at complete time only — rejected: work is already burned by then, and a claim-everything/complete-nothing session never trips it.
Store the pace policy in the motive charter — rejected: pacing is a per-run property and a charter-level budget cannot expire with the run, which the autopilot grant requires.
Default pacing ON for all existing ledgers — rejected: would retroactively block in-flight runs that were planned without a budget.

data.decision: When pacing is exhausted (no claimable unit remains for this session) and incomplete slices remain, hooks/stop-gate.mjs MUST allow the stop instead of blocking on incomplete slices, and MUST emit a directive (not an advisory) telling the operator to run the handoff skill and open a new session, naming the motive MAP.md path and the exact slice ids left.
